title: Quasi-isomorphism of the specified scalar tensor chain comparison
statement: Let ell be prime, E,L finite extensions of Q_ell and iota:E→L a coefficient embedding. For any scheme W and good complexes P,Q of completed E-coefficient sheaves (K-flat with flat terms), the specified map scalarTensorChain [lem-pur-integral-scalar-finite-comparison-models] is a quasi-isomorphism. Its source is ordinary scalar extension of the strict Roos tensor of P,Q; its target is the strict Roos tensor of their ordinary scalar extensions. The map is the prescribed scalarRoosMap followed by integralOperationsRoosMap of scalarTensorTower, without any choice of derived comparison.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 0941; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL; derived.tex Tag 08TC; Bhatt--Scholze, Proposition 3.5.1 (finite-free completion exchange).

proof.text: For each finite level n use the normalized ramified tensor-level isomorphism d:C_n≅D_m at some m≥n. Test morphisms from scalar-extended finite tensors using the scalar adjunction and finite tensor generator extensionality. Induction on m-n gives the generator formula for every recorded tower transition. The specified normalization of scalarTensorTower and d then proves alpha_m followed by d.inv is C(m→n), and d.inv followed by alpha_n is D(m→n). This uses no goodness hypothesis.

Apply the diagonal cone-transition homotopy to these two factorizations. Every sufficiently late transition in the mapping-cone tower is nullhomotopic and therefore zero in the derived category. The ringed strict-tower homotopy-limit theorem makes its derived-limit cone vanish. Compare this derived limit with the explicit strict Roos functor using its right-derived universal property; hence integralOperationsRoosMap alpha is a quasi-isomorphism.

A finite-free coefficient basis identifies ordinary scalar extension followed by restriction with a finite power functor, so scalar extension preserves countable products. Its canonical product comparison is invertible, and its additive biproduct comparison is invertible. The two prescribed coordinates of scalarRoosMap identify every degree with the composite of these isomorphisms, so scalarRoosMap is an isomorphism of complexes. Compose with the quasi-isomorphism of step 2. By definition this composite is exactly scalarTensorChain.
